facts.fact: E&M Magazine reports INTIC makes an 'Advanced Digital Signer' available on its portal, letting holders of accounts with state entities sign documents electronically and recipients verify authenticity.
INTIC president Lourino Chemane says the Advanced Digital Signer is used by ten civil service institutions.

MOZ.note: Only says civil servants lack training in emerging technologies; no programme stated.

facts.fact: An EY Mozambique partner, Bruno Dias, is quoted saying new companies offer data centre services in Mozambique: private clouds, hosting and housing (renting physical space to install servers).
E&M Magazine reports INCM's Universal Access Service Fund supports a rural connectivity project in 10 locations across named districts, with practical results far below expectations.

MOZ.note: Notes low digital literacy only; no programme or measured share.
No budget amount, statement or act on domestic financing.
Consultation is stated but not that it was online.
REG interconnects public institutions; no local government office is said to be on it.
INAGE data centres are not said to be for hire; hire offer is by unowned-stated new companies.
Only advice that continuity plans be made; no backup site named.

facts.fact: E&M Magazine reports INTIC has put out for public consultation its regulations on data centres and on cloud computing services.

MOZ.note: Internet in Schools project (300 schools planned) is a programme, not a share figure.
